ctx.x: And he was a little -- I don't know whether I said this before but when I ---he really didn't want me to join Nat because we had quite a good thing going. And I was under contract to him. I might have mentioned this before, but he finally said, okay, John, if you must go, because Nat was pretty good and making quite a bit of money at that time. And this was a step, financially for me, you know, a step forward financially for me. But musically where do you go from Art?

But any way, I wondered about it. I left him in St. Paul, Minnesota. I flew to California and joined Nat at the Tiffany Club, and I wondered how Art really felt about it. I knew he was a little peeved with me, and with Nat, but as soon as he came to California I looked up at night and there he was in the Tiffany to see. Because -- to see us. He loved Nat and he loved me. So every night he was there and when he became ill he stayed home quite a bit. And he had a chauffer by the name of -- he used to call him…

day and I would have dinner with him at Mike [Limens.] And I felt so sorry because he was just a shell of his former self. He would come up to my hotel room and just sit and I can remember Ben Webster, Harry Edison Addison, Dan Grissom Grisom, we would all lie and do everything, just stand on our heads just to make him laugh. And he -- because he had a hell of a sense of humor. But at this point we really couldn't get to him. I didn't --
